subject.title: Fork-per-issue from one warmed repo box

question: Should Clownfish adopt a warmed snapshot-fork workspace pool as a supported execution architecture, and if so which isolation and runtime contract should it guarantee?
rationale: The proposal changes worker provisioning and operational trust boundaries; source-level implementation cannot safely choose the runtime, fallback policy, and data-isolation guarantees without maintainer intent.

options.title: Approve a guarded pool design
options.body: Sponsor a design that keeps the current provisioning path as fallback and specifies immutable bases, disposable forks, secret isolation, invalidation, and observability before coding.

options.title: Keep isolated fresh provisioning
options.body: Retain the current per-job workspace model until measured setup cost warrants a supported pool and its operational ownership.

options.title: Prototype outside core workflow ownership
options.body: Validate the mitos or Crabbox integration as an external operator experiment before committing Clownfish to a permanent runtime contract.

recommendation.title: Approve a guarded pool design
recommendation.body: Sponsor a design that keeps the current provisioning path as fallback and specifies immutable bases, disposable forks, secret isolation, invalidation, and observability before coding.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged work is the closest identified recent contribution to Clownfish's bounded-concurrency workflow execution path.
